text: .1 Most convincingly associated with secondary malignancies are the various alkylating agents2-5 including the nitrosoureas, and the topoisomerase II inhibitor podophyllotoxin derivatives such as etoposide and teniposide.2,3,5,6 Leukaemias, particularly acute myeloid leukaemia, are the most common forms of sec- ondary disease.1-3 Leukaemia associated with alkylating agents usually occurs about 5 to 7 years after treatment, and is often preceded by a preleukaemic myelodysplasia.2,3 The nitrosoureas are associated with a relatively high frequency of secondary leu- kaemia, and busulfan and melphalan are considered to be more leukaemogenic than cyclophosphamide.3 Leukaemia associated with the podophyllotoxin derivatives has a shorter latency period of 2 to 3 years, with sudden onset and no myelodysplastic phase.2,3 Solid tumours can also occur as secondary malignan- cies and include bladder cancer associated with cyclophospha- mide used to treat non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma,4 and bone sarco- mas, and breast and lung cancers after the use of various alkylating agents.4,7 There is little evidence of carcinogenicity associated with antimetabolites such as methotrexate, although it has been sug- gested that they may act as co-carcinogens.8 Fludarabine therapy has been reported to be associated with the development of my- elodysplasia and acute myeloid leukaemias,9 although a review of the purine nucleoside analogues, cladribine and fludarabine, concluded that no significant increase in the risk of secondary malignancy had been shown, but also that long-term follow-up of patients was needed.10 Immunosuppression caused by antime- tabolites including methotrexate, cladribine, and fludarabine, may also allow the development of Epstein-Barr virus-related lymphoma.10,11 Platinum derivatives such as carboplatin and cisplatin have been found in large cohort studies12,13 to have a dose-response relationship with the development of secondary leukaemia. Combinations that may also be associated with leu- kaemias include cisplatin with doxorubicin,14 and other anthra- cycline-based regimens.15 Another drug that has been associated with the development of secondary malignancies is procar- bazine.3,4,16,17 Estimates of risk have varied very widely between studies, and have been calculated in various ways, making direct comparison impossible.
